Honestly, the first movie is kind of boring. Not a lot happens and it's mostly a family being on vacation with an occasional aside with a weird biker gang.

There's some stuff, but it's barely apocalyptic at all. It's just sort of plods along and doesn't really get interesting until the last 20 minutes or so, and even then it's not anywhere near what it became with Road Warrior.

It's cheaply made and it shows. It's a cult movie and Miller really doesn't have any idea how to pace things or handle a lot of the shots. It's almost like watching a student film really, a good student film, but not more than that. It barely ties into the sequels at all. The backstory established in Mad Max is barely relevant in the later films and everything you need to know that happens in it gets explained in the later films.

Mad Max, as much of a cult following as it has, is completely skipable. It's not a horrible movie, particularly the Aussie cut, but it's slow meandering, and doesn't have the budget to pull off it's bigger ideas. It really does seem like Mad Max and the other films take place in completely different worlds, not just the same one at a later date.

I say start with Road Warrior, it's where all the iconic imagery and the idea of what Max really is came from, then do Thunderdome and Fury Road after.

Watch the first one if you really get hooked, but it's kind of an afterthought that's really only for hardcore fans. It's badly paced, the director is still figuring out camerawork, and overall the only memorable for starting Gibson's career.

Road Warrior is badass, great film. Miller had his shit together when he shot that one. Thunderdome is campy and not as good, but catches a lot of shit that it doesn't deserve. It's a better movie than Mad Max is and gets a lot of flack just because Road Warrior was so much better.

Fury Road is grand. I liked it the most out of all of it, just because it's such a chaotic film that catches the spirit of the franchise better than even Road Warrior does. It also avoids the cheesy 80s elements that kind of drag down Road Warrior in some segments.

The game is it's own thing, it doesn't really tie into any of the movies directly, but it's best if you're familiar with the character before you play. It's the same character in the same world, but no story elements tie into anything you see in the films or vice versa. It's a self contained thing that doesn't really need the rest of it to stand on it's own.

That said, I'd say it's not really the best place to learn about Max or the world. You can play and enjoy it without having seen the films, there's nothing difficult to understand about anything if you don't. The setting and situation are all easy to understand without having seen the movies first, but you'll get more out of the games if you have seen at least some of the movies. Notably Road Warrior and to some extent Thunderdome. Having seen Fury Road doesn't hurt, but also doesn't really add anything to the game.

I recommend watching Road Warrior and Fury Road at least, and then playing the game. Thunderdome and Mad Max you can do without, especially Mad Max. Mad Max isn't a bad movie, but it doesn't tie into the sequels as much as you'd think and is kind of a b-movie level production that is crazy and has a lot of good ideas, but Miller wasn't experienced enough and didn't have the budget to really capitalize on them until the sequels.
I guess I should have clarified, I was asking about the most recent Mad Max. Nevertheless, I will add Road Warrior to my watchlist.
